key_insight: PatternBoost, when adapted with geometry-aware representations and search moves, can automate the discovery of stronger extremal constructions than prior hand-designed efforts.
engineering_relevance: The study shows that learning-guided search can accelerate lower-bound discovery for combinatorial geometry problems, informing algorithm design and hardness analysis.
method: Alternate local search with transformer-generated candidate constructions.
Use tailored instance encodings plus surrogate ranking before exact verification.
Inject modest expert-crafted diversity when automated search plateaus.
evidence_signal: On stabbing unit squares with axis-parallel lines, the method improved the best known lower bound from 3/2 to 20/13, and with structured staircase initialization to 14/9.
watch_item: Performance appears sensitive to representation quality and initial diversity, so naive encodings or search operators may fail or plateau early.
paper_title: Towards Learning-Guided Discovery of Extremal Geometric Constructions: A PatternBoost Study
